question: What is the main feature of Nigeria's current population structure?

options.C: A very low dependency ratio nationwide

explanation: Nigeria has a young population where children and youths make up the vast majority, creating a high dependency burden on the working-age population. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do rapid population growth and high fertility rates directly matter for frontline midwives?

options.A: They eliminate the need for community health education programs
options.B: They reduce the average workload in rural primary health clinics
options.C: They automatically guarantee higher national government budgets
options.D: They increase pressure on maternal and child health services

explanation: When population growth outpaces facility capacity, maternity centers experience severe strain, leading to overworked staff and stretched resources. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which organization first introduced formal family planning services in Nigeria back in 1957?

options.A: World Health Organization African Regional Office
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health Division of Population
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: Volunteers under the leadership of pioneers like Dr. Abimbola Silva formed the PPFN to start organized family planning clinics in Lagos. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h2)

question: How did early family planning pioneers in Nigeria successfully gain initial acceptance?

options.A: Enforcing mandatory birth limits for all married couples
options.B: Focusing heavily on child spacing and treating infertility
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign laws and imported mandates
options.D: Avoiding all contact with existing government hospitals

explanation: To overcome deep cultural and religious resistance, early advocates framed their work around maternal health, safe child spacing, and helping couples struggling with infertility. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h2)

question: In what year was Nigeria's first comprehensive National Population Policy officially launched?
explanation: The government launched the foundational National Population Policy in 1988 to address the challenges of rapid population growth on national development. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a key objective of the National Population Policy regarding fertility?

options.A: Empowering couples to achieve their desired family size safely
options.B: Eliminating the need for maternal and child health clinics
options.C: Imposing a strict national limit of two children per family
options.D: Banning all contraceptive use outside major urban areas

explanation: The policy focuses on voluntary spacing and planned families rather than forcing limits, emphasizing health and personal choice. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing Nigeria's population policy implementation?

options.B: Universal availability of surplus healthcare funding
options.C: Intermittent contraceptive commodity stockouts in clinics
options.D: Poor infrastructure and difficult rural road networks

explanation: Funding is rarely surplus; the sector often suffers from underfunding and relies heavily on unpredictable donor assistance. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is task-shifting an important strategy in modern Nigerian family planning?

options.A: It permanently removes midwives from community primary health care centers
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any supply chain management systems
options.C: It enables lower-cadre health workers to provide basic contraceptives where doctors are scarce
options.D: It ensures that only specialist physicians can distribute modern family planning methods

explanation: Task-shifting authorizes trained community health extension workers and nurses to offer specific contraceptive services, expanding access in rural areas. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h4)

question: What primary role do midwives play regarding national population policies?

options.A: They function exclusively as federal budget planners in the ministry
options.B: They serve as the vital bridge between policy targets and grassroots clinical delivery
options.C: They are restricted from discussing family planning during antenatal visits
options.D: They focus solely on surgical procedures in tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Midwives work directly with individuals and communities, translating broad national health goals into daily clinical care and counseling. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can a midwife in a rural Nigerian clinic actively support the National Population Policy?

options.A: Waiting exclusively for clients to ask for birth control without offering advice
options.B: Refusing to offer family planning services to young or unmarried women
options.C: Directing all pregnant women to travel abroad for routine antenatal care
options.D: Providing accurate contraceptive counseling and community health education

explanation: Educating clients and providing accessible, respectful family planning services directly helps reduce maternal mortality and supports healthy child spacing. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h5)
